title: Clouds Need Tiny Particles to Form
post_title: Clouds Need Tiny Particles to Form | QuantaTale
post_description: A cloud can begin with something as tiny as a speck of dust. Discover the science behind it. Sources: https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/clouds/how-clouds-form https://science.nasa.gov/kids/earth/how-do-clouds-form/ #Science #ScienceFacts #Education #QuantaTale
narration: Clouds may look weightless, but their droplets need a starting point. Water evaporates into invisible water vapour. When moist air rises, it expands and cools. Once it reaches saturation, water vapour can condense onto microscopic particles such as dust, sea salt or smoke. These are called cloud condensation nuclei. Countless tiny droplets or ice crystals gather to make a visible cloud. A cloud is not simply water vapour floating in the sky.
